subject.title: Feature: configurable LLM retry with backoff on transient errors (overloaded/529)

question: Should OpenClaw expose a public configurable main-LLM retry/backoff policy now, and should that contract live under provider request config, agent defaults, or remain built-in only?
rationale: The change adds public config surface and changes provider routing, auth-profile rotation, fallback timing, request latency, and availability semantics, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive product/API direction.

options.title: Approve One Retry Contract
options.body: Pick one canonical provider or agent-level retry shape and require schema, docs, runtime behavior, upgrade behavior, focused tests, and real proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Keep Built-In Only
options.body: Avoid a public retry knob for now and limit work to narrow built-in retry/fallback fixes with explicit idempotency boundaries.

options.title: Defer The Feature
options.body: Leave SDK retry, auth cooldown, cron retry, and fallback behavior as-is until maintainers decide the extra config surface is worth carrying.

recommendation.title: Approve One Retry Contract
recommendation.body: Pick one canonical provider or agent-level retry shape and require schema, docs, runtime behavior, upgrade behavior, focused tests, and real proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame and recent provider/failover history make vincentkoc the strongest routing owner for this API and runtime decision.
